U.S. economist Stephen Roach, who proposed the "Hong Kong is over" argument, recently wrote again that "the old Hong Kong is indeed over," questioning Hong Kong's economic dependence on the mainland and pointing out that the National Security Law has weakened Hong Kong's rule of law and freedoms. Acting Financial Secretary Wong Wai-lun today published an article in a newspaper, refuting Roach's remarks without naming him, stating that recently "some media commentaries have attempted to cast a negative outlook on Hong Kong," and that Hong Kong must correct the misinformation spread by "naysayers."

Wong Wai-lun today wrote an article refuting criticism that downplayed Hong Kong's prospects, pointing out that in the first half of this year, Hong Kong's initial public offering (IPO) fundraising amount doubled compared to the same period last year. He attended the listing ceremony of mainland optical module manufacturer Zhongji Innolight this morning, describing it as "the largest IPO project in Hong Kong's capital market in nearly seven years." (Photo from Wong Wai-lun's Facebook)

Wong Wai-lun today wrote an article in Sing Tao Daily titled "Hong Kong: Embracing a New Era of Opportunities," stating that recent media commentaries have attempted to cast a negative outlook on Hong Kong's prospects, ignoring Hong Kong's resilience and vitality and turning a blind eye to enormous opportunities. Hong Kong must refute such criticism with concrete actions, "correcting the misinformation spread by those naysayers."

He subsequently cited various data, stating that Hong Kong's economy has "strongly rebounded," including a turnaround from a contraction of 3.7% when the current government took office in 2022 to growth of 3.6% last year, while the first-quarter growth of 5.9% this year also represented the largest increase in five years. He noted that external trade has risen, with exports continuing to grow, and that in June this year, merchandise exports and imports increased by 53.4% and 45.4% year-on-year respectively. In the first half of this year, Hong Kong saw 87 IPOs with fundraising reaching HK$210.2 billion, nearly double that of the same period last year; as of the end of June, over 500 applications were still being processed.

Citing the 2026 Global Wealth Report, Wong Wai-lun pointed out that Hong Kong has become the world's largest cross-border wealth management centre; last year, Hong Kong-registered authorised funds recorded net inflows of HK$357 billion, and the number of family offices grew by more than 25% over the past two years. Hong Kong also continues to be ranked the world's freest economy, with its global competitiveness ranking rising to second place.

He concluded by stating that "some critics seem to be driven more by prejudice against China" than by objective analysis, that the criticism is neither evidence-based nor factual, and reiterated that investors and talent are full of confidence in Hong Kong.
